finding.summary: Arrow-key half of the overlay guard is asserted vacuously — `navigate` can never be called in this fixture
finding.evidence: `fetchDocuments` is mocked to `async () => []` (image-viewer.test.tsx:37), so `siblings` is empty in image-viewer.tsx:117-136 and both `prevId`/`nextId` are `undefined`. `go(undefined)` (image-viewer.tsx:138-141) short-circuits, so `navigate` is never called for ArrowRight whether or not `hasOpenOverlay()` guards it. The assertion `expect(navigate).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` at line 117 — commented "Arrow keys belong to the overlay too while it is open" — therefore holds even if the guard is deleted, and the arrow-key branch is presented as covered when it is not.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. fetchDocuments is mocked as `async () => []` (image-viewer.test.tsx:37) for the exact module the viewer imports (image-viewer.tsx:7, 112-116); the overlay test passes no token, so `enabled: !token` is true and the query resolves to []. Consequently `siblings` is [] (image-viewer.tsx:117-129), `index === -1`, and both prevId and nextId are undefined (image-viewer.tsx:131-136). The ArrowRight branch calls `go(nextId)` = `go(undefined)`, and `go` is `(id?: string) => id && navigate(...)` (image-viewer.tsx:138-141), which short-circuits without calling navigate. So `expect(navigate).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (image-viewer.test.tsx:117), captioned "Arrow keys belong to the overlay too while it is open" (line 115), passes identically whether or not the hasOpenOverlay() guard at image-viewer.tsx:158 exists — it cannot fail. `navigate` is a module-level vi.fn cleared in beforeEach (lines 15, 86), so no other call source exists. No other test in this file or the sibling __tests__ files exercises arrow keys with a non-empty sibling list, so the arrow-key half of the guard has no meaningful coverage while being presented as covered. The Esc half IS genuinely covered (lines 109-125, including the positive control at 122-124), so the defect is scoped to the arrow-key assertion. This is a vacuous assertion presented as coverage for a behavior branch — squarely in the test-adequacy lane, major severity. No refutation ground applies: the code is present exactly as described, reachable, and in scope.

verdict.reason: The viewer registers its keydown handler in capture phase deliberately (image-viewer.tsx:143-145, 163-164), but no test in the repository is sensitive to that choice. The single overlay test (image-viewer.test.tsx:109-125) renders a controlled `<Dialog open>` with no `onOpenChange` (L61-67), so the Radix dialog never closes or unmounts on Esc and `hasOpenOverlay()` (image-viewer.tsx:40-42) returns true in bubble phase just as in capture phase; the remaining cases (L88-93, L95-103, L131-139, L143-155) dispatch at `window`/an input with no closing overlay and pass in either phase. I searched beyond the reviewer's stated scope: only two test files reference the viewer at all, and the second (file-detail.test.tsx:84-88) mocks `ImageViewer` away; no test spies on `addEventListener` for it (only design-editor/date-format-preference tests do); the `popper-content-wrapper` hit in packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:1474 is an unrelated Playwright wait in the UI-hunter harness, not a viewer test; there is no e2e spec exercising Esc on the viewer. So no counterexample exists: reverting the third argument to bubble phase leaves the suite green, i.e. the behavior the change exists for is untested.
